'''Élie-Franck Okobo''' (born October 23, 1997) is a French professional [[basketball]] player for [[Élan Béarnais Pau-Lacq-Orthez]] of the [[LNB Pro A]]. A {{height|ft=6|in=3}} tall [[combo guard]], the [[Bordeaux]] native began his club career at age 16, joining local team [[JSA Bordeaux Basket|JSA Bordeaux]], for whom he saw limited playing time. Okobo subsequently competed for the [[reserve team|youth team]] of Élan Béarnais, reaching the [[:fr:Championnat de France de basket-ball Espoirs|LNB Espoirs]] title game in 2016. In the [[2016–17 Pro A season|2016–17 season]], he assumed a greater role with the senior team, and in the following year, he became a regular starter.

Okobo has represented France at international competition on multiple occasions. He was a key player for the under-20 team at the [[FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]], which he took part in twice, winning a bronze medal in [[2017 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship|2017]]. Okobo has also suited up for the [[France national basketball team|senior national team]] at [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Europe)|FIBA World Cup qualification]]. He has been considered one of the top international prospects, and a potential first-round selection, for the [[2018 NBA draft]].

==Early life and career==
Okobo was born in [[Bordeaux]], France to a Congolese father and French mother.<ref name="netsdaily">{{cite web|title=Did Sean Marks divert his plane to France for a look at Elie Okobo?|url=https://www.netsdaily.com/2018/3/18/17135986/did-sean-marks-divert-his-plane-to-france-for-a-look-at-elie-okobo|publisher=Nets Daily|accessdate=April 12, 2018|date=March 18, 2018}}</ref><ref name=interview>{{cite AV media|people=Okobo, Elie|date=January 20, 2018|title=Elie Okobo Interview|medium=Video|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PEgqK_h2FLY|location=[[Pau, Pyrénées-Atlantiques|Pau]]|publisher=DraftExpress}}</ref> He has one sister and two brothers: his older brother plays [[handball]] and competes in [[track and field]], while his younger brother plays basketball. Okobo's father also has basketball experience.<ref name=interview/> 

At age 16, Okobo joined [[JSA Bordeaux Basket]] of the [[Nationale Masculine 1]] (NM1), the [[amateur sports|amateur]] level [[French basketball league system|third-tier division]] of French basketball.<ref name="europecup">{{cite web|title=Pau-Lacq-Orthez youngster Okobo turning heads in FIBA Europe Cup|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europecup/16-17/news/pau-lacq-orthez-youngster-okobo-turning-heads-in-the-fiba-europe-cup|publisher=[[FIBA]]|accessdate=April 11, 2018|date=January 6, 2017}}</ref> He made his senior men's [[sports club|club]] debut on February 8, 2014, shooting 0-of-1 from the field in one minute of playing time against Basket Club Montbrison.<ref>{{cite web|title=Feb 8, 2014 – BC Montbrison Masculins vs. JSA Bordeaux Basket|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2014-02-08/BC-Montbrison-Masculins-at-JSA-Bordeaux-Basket/155078|publisher=[[RealGM]]|accessdate=April 7, 2018}}</ref> He scored his only points of the season, on March 8 versus [[JA Vichy-Clermont Métropole]], with 2 points.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mar 8, 2014 – JA Vichy vs. JSA Bordeaux Basket|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2014-03-08/JA-Vichy-at-JSA-Bordeaux-Basket/155139|publisher=[[RealGM]]|accessdate=April 7, 2018}}</ref> In four contests, he averaged 0.5 points and 0.3 steals per game, in 2.2 minutes per game.<ref name="realgm">{{cite web|title=Elie Okobo|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Elie-Okobo/Summary/65475|publisher=[[RealGM]]|accessdate=April 7, 2018}}</ref>

In the 2014–15 season, Okobo began playing for Espoirs Pau-Lacq-Orthez in the [[:fr:Championnat de France de basket-ball Espoirs|LNB Espoirs]] youth league.<ref name="espoirs1">{{cite web|title=Elie Okobo|url=http://www.lnbespoirs.fr/player/?code=A64880&lea=fraj&year=x1415#gamebygame|publisher=LNB Espoirs|accessdate=April 11, 2018}}</ref> In his debut on September 20, 2014, he chipped in 23 points and 4 steals as his team lost to Espoirs Châlons-Reims.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chalons-Reims – Pau-Lacq-Orthez 85–79|url=http://www.lnbespoirs.fr/game/gamebox.phtml?year=x1415&lea=fraj&code=8734|publisher=LNB Espoirs|accessdate=April 11, 2018|date=September 20, 2014}}</ref> On December 23, he scored a season-high 24 points, shooting 6-of-7 from the three-point line, in a 79–78 win over Espoirs Nancy.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nancy – Pau-Lacq-Orthez 78–79|url=http://www.lnbespoirs.fr/game/gamebox.phtml?year=x1415&lea=fraj&code=8872|publisher=LNB Espoirs|accessdate=April 11, 2018|date=December 23, 2014}}</ref> After 29 games, Okobo averaged 9.8 points, 3.0 rebounds, 1.9 assists, and 1.2 steals per game.<ref name=espoirs1/>

==Professional career==
===Élan Béarnais (2015–present)===
==== Youth success (2015–16) ====
On June 13, 2016, Okobo signed a three-year contract with [[Élan Béarnais Pau-Lacq-Orthez]] of the [[LNB Pro A]], the highest [[professional sports|professional]] division of France.<ref>{{cite web|title=Premier contrat pro pour Elie Okobo|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Basket/Actualites/Pau-orthez-premier-contrat-pro-pour-elie-okobo/694561|website=[[L'Équipe]]|accessdate=April 12, 2018|date=June 14, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Pau-Orthez signs Elie Okobo to a three-year contract|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/france/pro-a/202095/pau-orthez-signs-elie-okobo-to-a-three-year-contract.html|publisher=Sportando|accessdate=April 7, 2018|date=June 14, 2016}}</ref> Through the [[2015–16 Pro A season|2015–16 season]], he primarily played with Espoirs Pau-Lacq-Orthez in the youth league, seeing limited minutes for the senior team in the Pro A.<ref name="201516gl">{{cite web|title=Elie Okobo Game Logs: 2015–2016|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Elie-Okobo/GameLogs/65475/International/2016|publisher=[[RealGM]]|accessdate=April 12, 2018}}</ref><ref name="espoirs2">{{cite web|title=Elie Okobo|url=http://www.lnbespoirs.fr/player/?code=A64880&lea=fraj&year=x1516#home|publisher=LNB Espoirs|accessdate=April 12, 2018}}</ref> On Pau-Lacq-Orthez 56–102|url=http://www.lnbespoirs.fr/game/gamebox.phtml?year=x1516&lea=fraj&code=10924|publisher=LNB Espoirs|accessdate=April 12, 2018|date=October 6, 2015}}</ref> He made his Pro A Basket|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2015-10-24/Pau-Orthez-at-Paris-Levallois-Basket/216070|publisher=[[RealGM]]|accessdate=April 12, 2018}}</ref> On March 25, 2016, Okobo erupted for 34 points and 10 rebounds, both season-bests, in a youth league win over Espoirs Le Havre.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pau-Lacq-Orthez – Le Havre 100–57|url=http://www.lnbespoirs.fr/game/gamebox.phtml?year=x1516&lea=fraj&code=11129|publisher=LNB Espoirs|date=March 25, 2016}}</ref> In the following week against [[AS Monaco Basket]], he scored 5 points—his first and only of the Pro A season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Apr 4, 2016 – AS Monaco Basket vs. Pau-Orthez|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2016-04-04/AS-Monaco-Basket-at-Pau-Orthez/216703|publisher=[[RealGM]]}}</ref> By the end of the season, Espoirs Pau-Lacq-Orthez had assists, and 2.2 steals per game.<ref name=espoirs2/>

==== Increased role (2016–17) ====
[[File:Elie Okobo 2 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Okobo (right) tries to steal the ball from [[Tweety Carter]] (left) in 2017.]]
In the [[2016–17 Pro A season|2016–17 season]], Okobo played sparingly in LNB Espoirs, instead receiving significant minutes off the bench for Pau-Orthez in the Pro A.<ref name=realgm/><ref name="espoirs3">{{cite web|title=Elie Okobo|url=http://www.lnbespoirs.fr/player/?code=A64880&lea=fraj&year=x1617|publisher=LNB Espoirs|accessdate=April 13, 2018}}</ref> On September 24, 2016, he made his season debut in the Pro A, recording 5 points, 2 rebounds, and 2 assists against [[Cholet Basket]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Sep 24, 2016 – Cholet Basket vs. Pau-Orthez|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2016-09-24/Cholet-Basket-at-Pau-Orthez/240547|publisher=[[RealGM]]|accessdate=April 13, 2018}}</ref> In his second appearance of the LNB Espoirs season, Okobo posted a [[double (basketball)|double-double]] of 21 points and 12 rebounds on October 15 versus Espoirs Gravelines-Dunkerque.<ref>{{cite web|title=Gravelines-Dunkerque – Pau-Lacq-Orthez 89–91|url=http://www.lnbespoirs.fr/game/gamebox.phtml?year=x1617&lea=fraj&code=11556|publisher=LNB Espoirs|accessdate=April 13, 2018|date=October 15, 2016}}</ref> On October 25, he debuted in the [[FIBA Europe Cup]], the [[European professional club basketball system|fourth-tier]] inter-continental European competition, notching 6 points and 2 rebounds in a win over [[BC Tartu|Tartu]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Oct 25, 2016 – Tartu Ulikool Rock vs. Pau-Orthez|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2016-10-25/Tartu-Ulikool-Rock-at-Pau-Orthez/252546|publisher=[[RealGM]]|accessdate=April 13, 2018}}</ref> Later in the week, Okobo had another double-double in the LNB Espoirs, adding 18 points and 13 assists, along with 6 rebounds, against Espoirs Orleans.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pau-Lacq-Orthez – Orleans 78–75|url=http://www.lnbespoirs.fr/game/gamebox.phtml?year=x1617&lea=fraj&code=11578|website=October 29, 2016|publisher=LNB Espoirs|accessdate=April 13, 2018}}</ref> On November 28, he scored 11 points in a 96–76 loss for his first career double-digit scoring effort in the Pro A.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nov 28, 2016 – Pau-Orthez vs. Chalon-Sur-Saone|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2016-11-28/Pau-Orthez-at-Chalon-Sur-Saone/245354|publisher=[[RealGM]]|accessdate=April 13, 2018}}</ref> 

Okobo recorded a season-high 20 points, 6 rebounds, 10 assists, and 1 turnover in a 101–66 victory over [[BK JIP Pardubice|JIP Pardubice]] in the second round of the FIBA Europe Cup on December 13.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pau-Lacq-Orthez v BK Pardubice|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europecup/16-17/1412/Pau-Lacq-Orthez-BK-Pardubice#tab=boxscore|publisher=[[FIBA]]|accessdate=April 14, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=The week's big numbers: Chikoko can't miss, Gagic in record-state-of-mind|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europecup/16-17/news/the-week-s-big-numbers-chikoko-cant-miss-gagic-in-record-state-of-mind|publisher=[[FIBA]]|accessdate=April 14, 2018|date=December 15, 2016}}</ref> He had another notable performance on January 24, 2017 against [[Alba Fehérvár]], scoring 10 points and hitting a game-winning three-pointer with under 10 seconds left to send his team to the FIBA Europe Cup Round of 16.<ref>{{cite web|title=Okobo's game winner dagger for Pau-Lacq Orthez|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europecup/16-17/videos/Okobo-s-game-winner-dagger-for-Pau-Lacq-Orthez|publisher=[[FIBA]]|accessdate=April 14, 2018|date=January 25, 2017}}</ref> He scored 8 points in the fourth quarter alone, with starting point guard [[D. J. Cooper]] being ejected in the final minutes of the game.<ref>{{cite web|title=Okobo's heroics in Hungary send Pau-Lacq-Orthez to Round of 16|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europecup/16-17/news/okobo-s-heroics-in-hungary-send-pau-lacq-orthez-to-round-of-16|publisher=[[FIBA]]|accessdate=April 14, 2018|date=January 24, 2017}}</ref> On February 5, 2017, Okobo scored a season-best 15 points, with 5 rebounds and 4 assists, in a Pro A win over Élan Chalon.<ref>{{cite web|title=Feb 5, 2017 – Chalon-Sur-Saone vs. Pau-Orthez|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2017-02-05/Chalon-Sur-Saone-at-Pau-Orthez/245794|publisher=[[RealGM]]|accessdate=April 14, 2018}}</ref> He closed the season averaging 4.6 points, 2.1 rebounds, and 1.5 assists per game in the Pro A, and 8.2 points, 3.3 rebounds, and 2.1 assists per game in the FIBA Europe Cup.<ref name=realgm/> Okobo was the runner-up for the [[LNB Pro A Best Young Player]] award, which was won by [[Frank Ntilikina]] of [[SIG Basket|SIG Strasbourg]].<ref>{{cite web|title=DJ Cooper meilleur joueur de Pro A, Elie Okobo 2e meilleur espoir|url=http://www.larepubliquedespyrenees.fr/2017/05/18/basket-dj-cooper-meilleur-joueur-de-pro-a-elie-okobo-2e-meilleur-espoir,2124317.php|website=La République des Pyrénées|accessdate=April 7, 2018|language=French|date=May 18, 2017}}</ref>

==== Breakout season (2017–18) ====
In his first game of the [[2017–18 Pro A season|2017–18 season]], Okobo made his starting lineup debut in the Pro A on September 23, 2017, chipping in 14 points and 8 assists to help defeat [[Élan Chalon]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Sep 23, 2017 – Pau-Orthez vs. Chalon-Sur-Saone|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2017-09-23/Pau-Orthez-at-Chalon-Sur-Saone/273879|publisher=[[RealGM]]|accessdate=April 18, 2018}}</ref> On October 7, he led all scorers with 21 points and 3 steals against [[HTV Basket]].<ref>{{cite web|title=l'Elan Béarnais corrige Hyères-Toulon|url=http://www.larepubliquedespyrenees.fr/2017/10/07/direct-suivez-le-choc-elan-bearnais-hyeres-toulon-ce-samedi-a-20h,2191869.php|website=La République des Pyrénées|accessdate=April 18, 2018|language=French|date=October 7, 2017}}</ref> Okobo had another notable performance on December 10, posting a team-high 23 points in a win over [[Levallois Metropolitans]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Pau se fait plaisir face à Levallois|url=http://www.basketactu.com/pau-se-fait-plaisir-face-a-levallois-117077/|publisher=BasketActu|accessdate=April 18, 2018|language=French|date=December 10, 2017}}</ref> He once again eclipsed the 20-point barrier on February 3, 2018 versus [[ASVEL Basket]], scoring 24 points to lead Pau-Orthez to victory.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Rutard|first1=Sacha|title=Pau s’offre un exploit à l’ASVEL, Elie Okobo score 24 points|url=https://www.basketeurope.com/livenews-fr/420372/pau-soffre-un-exploit-a-lasvel-elie-okobo-score-24-points/|publisher=Basket Europe|accessdate=April 18, 2018|language=French|date=February 3, 2018}}</ref>
On February 10, Okobo scored a career-high 30 points, along with 8 assists and 4 rebounds, in a 105–93 win over Élan Chalon.<ref>{{cite web|title=Feb 10, 2018 – Chalon-Sur-Saone vs. Pau-Orthez|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2018-02-10/Chalon-Sur-Saone-at-Pau-Orthez/294632|publisher=[[RealGM]]|accessdate=April 12, 2018}}</ref> The performance earned him Player of the Week honors from the website [[Eurobasket.com]].<ref name="pow">{{cite web|title=French ProA round 20 best performance: Elie-Franck Okobo|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/France/news/522703/French-ProA-round-20-best-performance:-Elie-Franck-Okobo|publisher=[[Eurobasket.com]]|accessdate=April 12, 2018|date=February 13, 2018}}</ref> He announced plans to enter the [[2018 NBA draft]] on April 11, saying, "I'm progressing every day and I see how I'm continuing to improve. I am very happy with the training I have received at Pau-Lacq-Orthez, and I know I will improve even more with NBA conditions and NBA training."<ref name="draft">{{cite web|last1=Givony|first1=Jonathan|title=French guard Elie Okobo enters NBA draft|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/23114608/elie-okobo-france-enters-nba-draft|publisher=[[ESPN]]|accessdate=April 18, 2018|date=April 11, 2018}}</ref> At the time, [[ESPN]] considered him to be a possible first-round selection, and three weeks later, analyst [[David Aldridge]] projected him as a late first-round or early second-round prospect.<ref name=draft/><ref>{{cite web|last1=Aldridge|first1=David|title=No shortage of NBA-ready guard prospects in 2018 Draft class|url=http://www.nba.com/da-big-board-guards-2018-draft|publisher=[[National Basketball Association|NBA]]|accessdate=April 29, 2018|date=April 2, 2018}}</ref> With Pau-Orthez, Okobo reached the playoffs as the eight-seed. On May 23, during Game 1 of the series against first-seeded [[AS Monaco Basket|Monaco]], Okobo scored a career-high 44 points in a 99–97 loss.<ref>[http://www.basketusa.com/news/499874/alors-que-la-draft-approche-elie-okobo-44-points-frappe-tres-fort-face-a-monaco/]</ref> That game would help Okobo's draft stock rise from a likely second round pick to a potential mid-first round selection. At the June 11 international draft day deadline, Okobo would be one of only 11 truly international prospects to remain in the 2018 NBA Draft.

==National team career==
Okobo was a member of the French under-20 national basketball team, making his first international appearance at the [[2016 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]] in [[Finland]]. He had his best performance of the event on July 23, 2017, notching 23 points, 7 rebounds, and 4 steals in a 74–60 victory over Finland.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jul 23, 2016 – Finland vs. France|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/national/boxscore/2016-07-23/Finland-at-France/239384|publisher=[[RealGM]]|accessdate=April 18, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Elie-Franck Okobo|url=http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/114155/sid/12457/tid/282/tid2//_/2016_FIBA_U20_European_Championship/index.html|publisher=[[FIBA]]|accessdate=April 18, 2018}}</ref> He was the third-leading scorer at the tournament, averaging 18.9 points, 3.9 rebounds, 1.6 assists, and 1.9 steals per game, shooting .429 from the three-point line.<ref name=realgm/> He also played with France's Under-20 junior national team, at the [[2017 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]], where he won a bronze medal. He averaged 12.3 points, 3.3 rebounds, and 4.0 assists per game at the tournament.<ref>[http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/rpp//q/%20Elie-Franck%20OKOBO/pid//_//players.html Elie-Franck OKOBO (FRA).]</ref>
